title: My open source project is brand new and already has contributors. Here's what I did.
why_read: A personal narrative about structuring a new open source project to attract first-time contributors during Hacktoberfest, useful mainly as soft community-management advice.
analysis: The author, a developer relations professional, reflects on making their new self-hosted AI support tool approachable to new open-source contributors. The actual project, answerLoops, automates community question-answering by searching a team's docs and having a second AI agent verify the drafted answer before a human approves it. The post's practical value is more about onboarding and labeling practices for open source maintainers than deep technical content. It's a reasonable but fairly generic piece of advice dressed up with a project showcase.
